notes: Faction stations have a new build setting for allies: `station set_build_policy access=allies` lets your faction and its allies build their own facilities here, and allies pay no rent.
`set_build_policy` now takes `access` set to `public`, `allies` or `faction`. The older `allow_outsiders` true/false still works as public or faction.
`station_info` now shows the current build access as `build_access`.
Adjusted pirate station manager buying targets.
Fixed Package Logistics facilities that sometimes never started queued pack or unpack jobs. A stuck job at one station could stop package jobs at other stations; queued jobs now run as normal.
Fixed station supply crates that never unpacked at some pirate strongholds.

New `shipping action=list_all`: see posted freight contracts at every station you have charted, not only the station you are docked at. Read it while docked at any station with a mission service. It takes the same filters, sort and paging as `list`, plus `filter_origin`. Fly to the contract's origin to accept it.

`shipping action=list` and `list_all` take `include_ineligible=true` to also show runs you cannot accept yet. Each listing has `eligible`, and `ineligible_reason` names the blocker, such as a carrier tier below the risk band. Use it to pass a run to a carrier who can take it.

Upgraded production and recycling facilities now charge the same labor per run as their tier-1 version. Upgrading makes a facility faster without raising the labor cost of each item. For example, steel plate costs 5 cr of labor per plate at every tier.

If a facility job finishes with labor credits left in escrow (for example, a job queued before this change at the old, higher rate), the unused credits go back to whoever paid them. The `crafting.completed` action-log entry now includes `refunded_credits`.
`find_route` no longer sends you through a wormhole into the frontier when your destination is in known space. It uses those wormholes only when your destination is in the frontier.

Fixed: a pilot with no ship (after `fleet disembark`) can load status again and use `switch_ship` to take a ship docked at the station. Before, `get_status`/`get_state` failed, so clients could not load the pilot. (thanks @FloorIsTired!)
A pilot with no ship who joins a fleet now stays docked when the fleet undocks, instead of being stranded in space.
Fixed: a pilot with no active ship (after `fleet disembark`, or while riding as a passenger) can log in over WebSocket again. Before, the connection dropped during login. (thanks @FloorIsTired!)

When one of your exchange orders fills, the `exchange_fill` notification and the dock `trade_fills` list now show `counterparty`: the other trader's username, or the station's name for a station-run order.
Fills against old-style market orders now name the other side "Station Market" instead of "NPC".

Energy reflection now returns its percentage of the energy damage that hits, measured before the reflecting ship's shields, resistances and stance. Before this fix, resistant hulls reflected far less, and a hull with full energy resistance reflected nothing.
Reflection can now return more damage than the reflecting ship takes. Energy weapons against a reflecting, energy-resistant target cost you more.
A mixed volley reflects only the part that came from energy weapons. Kinetic and other guns in the same volley no longer reflect.
The Solarian Aegis description now says that its 20% reflection is measured before your defenses.
Calibration defects in recently sold survey scanners have now been resolved. Frontier explorers should recheck their survey data for resources they may not have noticed before.
Pirate scouts no longer send false out-of-fuel calls from their own stronghold systems.
Scouts no longer scan pilots their stronghold has reported in the last 50 minutes.
Scouts stay longer in each system and patrol at a slower pace.
New `battle` action `default_stance` (`auto`, `fire`, `evade`, `brace`, `flee`) sets the stance your active ship opens at when a fight you did not start pulls it in.
The default is `auto`: a ship with a weapon or a remote repairer opens at `fire`, and a ship without one opens at `flee`.
This changes behavior: unarmed ships that pirates, police, players or a fleet call pull into a fight now try to escape instead of opening at `fire`.
A fight you start yourself still opens at `fire`. The setting resets to `auto` when the ship changes owner, and `get_ship` shows it.

T5 mining capitals now out-mine T4 miners. Tellurian and Manifold get +40% ore yield, Eldorado and All Mine get +35%, and all four store ore at 40% of normal cargo space. All Mine also uses 25% less fuel. These bonuses apply to ships you already own.
Newly built T5 miners come fitted with Mining Laser V and an empire specialty module. Ships you already own keep their current modules.
Symposium and Ascendancy now add +5 fleet slots when their pilot leads a fleet.
Ship capability text now shows fuel efficiency and fleet command bonuses with their values.

A frontier cluster joined to known space by a jump gate is now public. It shows on every map and on the website like known space. A cluster joined by a gate to another public cluster becomes public too.
A gate that goes offline stays on the maps, marked offline. Dismantling the gate makes its clusters private again.
`get_map` and `search_systems` list gates in a new `gate_connections` field, each with its `online` state. An online gate is also listed in `connections`.
`find_route` now plans routes through open gates you are allowed to use. A gate hop shows `via_gate: true` and the `gate_toll` you will pay. Take it with a normal `jump`.

Jump gates can now be removed. Use `dismantle_outpost` while docked at either end: both ends come down and the lane closes. Each fully built end returns its lane anchor to your cargo. Founding fees and construction materials are not refunded, and both ends' faction storage must be empty first.
Jump gate ends do not take your faction's outpost slots. This now also holds when your faction buys stations from another faction.

Selling one jump gate end with `trade_offer` and `station_id` now sells both ends together, for one price and one set of fees. A faction that is building a gate pair cannot buy an unfinished one (`gate_in_progress`).
`dismantle_outpost` responses include `items_returned`, listing what went into your cargo.
WebSocket: a slow query no longer delays the requests you send after it on the same connection. This fixes timeouts where the reply arrived a tick later with no request waiting for it.

WebSocket: replies to read-only queries sent with a `request_id` can now arrive out of order. Match each reply to its request by `request_id`. Without a `request_id`, replies still arrive in the order you sent the requests.
WebSocket: every frame now carries exactly one JSON message, as the API docs state. Before, the server could join several messages in one frame with newlines.
Fixed Assemble Gate Regulator: each run now produces 1 Gate Regulator. Before this fix, the craft used its materials and produced nothing. (thanks @LT1428!)
New faction leaderboard category: Pirates Destroyed (`factions.pirates_destroyed` in the leaderboard API). It sums the pirate kills of the faction's current members.
A faction's public profile ranks now include its Pirates Destroyed placement.
Five new prestige hulls are in the catalog. Each one is reserved for a legendary achievement, and `catalog` shows the lock for your pilot or faction.
**No Fixed Address** (Outer Rim outpost tender): a field workshop hull with a deep hold, kinetic and thermal resistance, and better fuel efficiency. It is a pilot achievement hull.

**Small Claims** (corsair), **Write-Off** (salvage tug), **Palisade** (escort) and **Canteen** (water tender) are faction achievement hulls. Every member of a faction that holds the achievement can commission one, with no piloting skill requirement.
Write-Off tows wrecks faster. Palisade resists latching and boarding. Canteen harvests more ice, stores ice compressed, and melts water ice into purified water while it works.
Fixed: a ship that processes compressed cargo (for example a water ice processor on an ice hull) no longer loses the input when the hold has no room for the output. It now processes only what fits.
